accuracy.evidence: Every calculation was recomputed: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl gives 679 − 864 = −185 kJ/mol (measured ΔH for 2HCl(g) is −184.6 kJ/mol); CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O gives 2648 − 3466 = −818 kJ/mol (measured about −802 kJ/mol with gaseous water, the gap explained as mean bond energies); N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ gives 2253 − 2346 = −93 kJ/mol (measured −92); 2HI → H₂ + I₂ gives 598 − 587 = +11 kJ/mol (measured about +9 kJ/mol with gaseous iodine). Bond energies (H–H 436, Cl–Cl 243, H–Cl 432, C–H 413, O=O 498, C=O 805 in CO₂, O–H 464, N≡N 945, N–H 391, H–I 299, I–I 151 kJ/mol) were checked against the OCR/Edexcel GCSE data sheets and the RSC Data Book; the method follows AQA GCSE Chemistry 4.5.1.3.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented misconceptions (Boo 1998; Barker and Millar 2000) that bond breaking releases energy and that fuels store energy (step 1 prediction, step 2 prediction 'Breaking the bonds in methane', challenge 'breakout' and 'store'), plus the calculation slips named in the adult text: made − broken (step 3 'flip' cards, step 5 line 3 of the ammonia answer, challenge 'flip'), missing coefficients (step 3 'times' cards +247, +1080, −288; step 5 HCl answer), and reading +ΔH as exothermic (step 5 HI answer, challenge 'up').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbonde is built on this topic's own mechanism: bonds are pulled apart one at a time with an energy-in tally, free atoms are dragged together to form H–Cl with an energy-out tally, bond counts are entered for each bond type in a balanced equation, and an energy ladder rises by the bonds broken to a 'separate atoms' level and falls by the bonds made. flaghpack (hand warmer) and the exothermic/endothermic energy visual show only the overall ΔH; flagsigma and flagcov draw bonds but never tally energy. lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the sign rule by doing it: each break adds to 'in', each make adds to 'out', and the step 1 finish reads 'In 679, out 864. More out than in, so ΔH = −185 kJ/mol: exothermic.' In step 4 the ladder shows the products ending below the reactants only when the out arrow is longer than the in arrow, and the endothermic HI case lands above. Feedback confirms afterwards (e.g. 'Too low. Only 864 kJ is given out: 679 − 864 = −185').

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each have a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: 'Breaking a bond gives energy out' (step 1 tallies energy in for every break), 'The energy from burning methane comes from breaking methane's bonds' (step 2 totals show 2648 in and 3466 out, so the release comes from making C=O and O–H), and 'endothermic' when making releases more (step 3 shows a negative ΔH).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; each wrong option has its own message: 'breakout' (breaking always takes energy in), 'free' (every bond needs energy, bond energies are measured), 'flip' (sign swapped: 1200 − 1500 = −300), 'add' (subtract, do not add), 'store' (energy is not stored in the fuel), 'up' (positive ΔH puts products above), 'level' (level means ΔH = 0) and 'mass' (mass is conserved; table values are averages).

readability.evidence: Learner kid text measured grade 4.2 (limit 6.5) and adult 9.5 (limit 9.5), with short sentences that put the rule first ('ΔH is the energy in minus the energy out.'). The step 3 and step 5 lab text was raised from 13 px to 14 px after the 360 px screenshots, and canvas labels use plain words (in, out, separate atoms) rather than symbols alone.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph states a rule or the methane example; the adult paragraphs give the standards, the definition, three worked calculations, the named mistakes and what each lab step does. The content gate found no filler phrases, and the explanation is under 12% the same as Exothermic and endothermic reactions and Designing a hand warmer or cold pack.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px wide screenshots in light and dark themes for every step before and after Show me: atoms and molecule tap areas are 140 × 60 px, count tiles 56 px, ΔH cards 52 px and worked-answer lines 46 px; the products knob was moved to the right end of its line after the screenshot showed it covering the label. In dark mode the bond lines and in/out colours switch to lighter tones (#cbd5e1, #fb923c, #22d3ee) for contrast. The walkthrough passed on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Break H–H, Break Cl–Cl, Make H–Cl; count buttons 1–4 with labels such as '4 C–H bonds'; ΔH buttons; products −100, −10, +10, +100 and Check level; Line 1–3 buttons whose labels read the line. The canvas aria-label is updated after every action, including each products move, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme on desktop and iPhone 13.
